done_when: An After entry may name another story's task as KEY/TASK (for example TURN-1/T4): forge next lists the task as ready, and forge task start starts it, only once that other task's pull request has merged, and both say plainly which task it waits for. A story doc whose After names a task that doesn't exist in that story's plan is refused as malformed, the same way an unknown same-story task is. The skill's plan-writing guidance mentions the form. Command-level tests cover waiting, starting after the other task merges, and an unknown task.

findings.body: The prior gap remains. When a story is planned before TURN-1/T4 merges and its first task depends on T4, this check permits starting after the merge, but the checkout still lacks T4's code. In src/forge/task.py:140, an unlanded plan selects the original story branch as the base; lines 181–182 create the task from that base without incorporating the fetched default branch. Start from the updated default branch while carrying the approved planning files, or incorporate that branch before creating the task.
findings.title: Start dependent tasks with the other story's merged code

findings.body: The prior malformed-document gap remains. Qualified references are checked only when top is supplied, but src/forge/story.py:501 still calls parse(text) without it. The real PR command invokes this gate at src/forge/prcheck.py:171, so an otherwise valid approved document naming TURN-1/T9 is not rejected as malformed when TURN-1 has no T9, although an unknown same-story task is rejected. Validate cross-story references using the PR's commit context and add a command-level refusal test through forge hook pr-check.
findings.title: Not done: An After entry may name another story's task as KEY/TASK (for example TURN-1/T4): forge next lists the task as ready, and forge ""

findings.body: The prior test gap remains. TURN-1/T4 is never approved or started: the test checks waiting while it has no state, then directly writes the merged-state receipt onto main. It therefore cannot detect incorrectly releasing a started but unmerged dependency or starting without the dependency's merged code. Approve and start T4 through Forge, assert both commands still wait, merge its actual task branch with a code change, then assert readiness, successful start, and that the dependent checkout contains that change. Include a first-task dependency scenario; merging SHOP/SAVE beforehand bypasses the stale-base defect.
findings.title: Not done: Test waiting for a started cross-story task and starting after its merge

why: A plan's After column can only name tasks in the same story, so a task that must wait for another story's task shows as ready in forge next and the agent has to hold it by hand
